clauses: Report the signed difference: type average minus the mean of the per-type averages.
Report the absolute difference between each type's average and the mean of the per-type averages.
readings: For each event type (`event.type`), matching budget lines to their events through `budget.link_to_event`, what is the average spent-to-budgeted ratio (`spent` / `amount`) across its budget lines, ignoring missing values? Also show how far each type's average is from the mean of the per-type averages. Report the signed difference: type average minus the mean of the per-type averages.

For each event type (`event.type`), matching budget lines to their events through `budget.link_to_event`, what is the average spent-to-budgeted ratio (`spent` / `amount`) across its budget lines, ignoring missing values? Also show how far each type's average is from the mean of the per-type averages. Report the absolute difference between each type's average and the mean of the per-type averages.
queries:
WITH type_avg AS (
    SELECT e.type AS type,
           AVG(CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / b.amount) AS avg_ratio
    FROM budget b
    JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL
      AND b.amount IS NOT NULL
      AND b.amount <> 0
    GROUP BY e.type
)
SELECT type,
       avg_ratio,
       avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM type_avg) AS diff_from_mean
FROM type_avg;
WITH type_avg AS (
    SELECT e.type AS type, AVG(b.spent * 1.0 / b.amount) AS avg_ratio
    FROM event e
    JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL AND b.amount IS NOT NULL AND b.amount <> 0
    GROUP BY e.type
)
SELECT type, avg_ratio, ABS(avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM type_avg)) AS abs_diff
FROM type_avg;
